title: Add trace span annotations for cache events (prefix/KV) to correlate with latency
author: Samir Qureshi
body:
Summary: This PR adds low-cardinality trace annotations for prefix cache + KV cache events so we can correlate cache behavior (hit/miss, miss reason, reuse depth) with request latency in traces without introducing high-cardinality metrics. Motivation: We have solid cache counters/histograms now, but during regressions it’s still hard to answer: “did p99 spike because cache misses increased, because misses are TTL/version related, or because we’re evicting under pressure?” Traces already include latency breakdowns; adding carefully-scoped span attributes/events lets oncall and runtime engineers connect the dots for individual slow requests and then pivot back to aggregate dashboards.

Design constraints / privacy & cardinality: - No prompt text and no prompt hashes. - No tenant_id/route_id/model_version in the trace annotations (those are already present in gateway/request context spans where allowed, and we don’t want to duplicate or widen propagation). - Only emit annotations when the span is recording (i.e., sampled), so we don’t add overhead to non-sampled requests. - All values are either booleans, enums, or pre-defined buckets.

What’s included: 1) Prefill span annotations: - Adds an event on the request span at end of prefill: event name: cache.prefill.summary - attributes: cache.prefix.hit (bool), cache.prefix.reused_tokens_bucket (enum), cache.prefix.reuse_ratio_bucket (enum), cache.kv.reused_blocks_bucket (enum), cache.kv.miss_reason (enum; only set when miss), cache.wasted_prefill_tokens_bucket (enum), cache.eviction_pressure (enum: none|low|high) 2) Decode span annotations: - Adds cache.decode.kv_cache status when decode starts (hit vs miss-driven recompute) to help explain decode tail latency when prefill was cheap but decode was expensive. 3) Trace safety guardrails: - All annotations are behind: runtime.cache_telemetry.trace_annotations_enabled (default: true in staging/canary, false in prod until rollout gate flips) - Emission checks span.is_recording() to avoid extra work when tracing is not sampled - Bucket mappings live in a single file (shared with metric bucket definitions where possible) to avoid drift.

Implementation notes: - We attach annotations to the existing request root span (redwood.request) and the prefill child span (redwood.prefill) when present. If spans are absent (tracing disabled), the instrumentation is a no-op. - Miss reason uses the same enum as the metrics work (capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, unknown). - “wasted prefill” in traces uses the same bucketization as the metric, computed from the prefill accounting that already exists; we do not introduce per-token logging.

Testing: - Unit tests validate bucket mapping boundaries and enum serialization. - Integration test extends the cache-metrics test harness to assert trace annotations appear for sampled spans (and not for non-sampled). - Manual: verified in staging with trace UI that cache.prefill.summary event shows up and can be filtered by miss_reason.

Perf/overhead: - Incremental overhead measured in perf-canary is within noise when tracing is disabled or not sampled; for sampled traces, additional allocations are bounded (string constants + small attribute set). - We intentionally avoid per-request dynamic strings; event names/keys are static constants.

Rollout plan: - Land behind flag (this PR). - Enable in staging immediately. - Enable in perf-canary + a small prod canary cell (Connor O’Brien to flip) after 24h stability. - If we see any trace volume or CPU regressions, roll back via config flag.

Screenshots/links: - Trace UI example (staging): internal link redwood-tracing://staging/trace/9b3d... (see comment). - Related: PR-18421/22/23/24 for cache metrics + wasted prefill; PR-18425 for sampling/rate limits.

Checklist: - [x] No high-cardinality labels/attributes added - [x] No prompt material logged - [x] Guarded by is_recording() - [x] Tests for bucketing + integration trace assertion - [x] Release note not required (flagged off by default in prod)

Review discussion highlights: Omar requested reusing the miss-reason enum from metrics to keep taxonomy stable and asked to ensure we don’t attach model_version in trace attrs; updated accordingly. Nadia asked for explicit bucket enums instead of raw token counts; updated to use *_bucket fields only. Allison requested a single “prefill summary” event rather than multiple events to reduce trace noise; consolidated events into one summary event and kept decode annotation minimal.

Outcome: Merged (squash) into main. Follow-up: once enabled in prod canary, SRE/Observability will add a saved trace query for cache.miss_reason=version_mismatch to accelerate triage (tracked in ENG-4824 notes).
commits: runtime/tracing: add cache annotation helper + bucket enums
runtime/cache: emit cache.prefill.summary trace event (prefix + KV)
runtime/cache: add decode span annotation for KV reuse status
tests: add unit tests for bucket mapping + enum serialization
integration: extend cache instrumentation test to assert trace annotations
ci_checks: integration-tests — pass (re-run once; initial failure due to flaky trace exporter timeout)
review_conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Love the direction. Two asks: (1) reuse the existing MissReason enum (don’t re-declare strings), and (2) please confirm we’re not adding model_version/route_id as span attrs here. Those are already on the gateway span and we don’t want to widen propagation.

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated to import MissReason from cache metrics module and map to a stable string set. Also removed the earlier model_version attr; now only the cache-specific buckets/enums are attached. Added a comment explaining why.

Nadia Rahman (review): +1 on keeping this out of metrics. For traces, can we avoid raw token counts? Buckets only please; otherwise people will start filtering by exact values and we’ll get pseudo-cardinality in tracing storage.
Samir Qureshi (author): Done. Switched to reused_tokens_bucket / reuse_ratio_bucket / wasted_prefill_tokens_bucket. Raw counts remain local variables only.

Allison Grant (review): Request: please collapse multiple events into a single prefill summary event; otherwise traces get noisy and hard to scan during incident triage. Also ensure we only emit when span.is_recording().
Samir Qureshi (author): Consolidated into cache.prefill.summary with ~6 attrs and gated on is_recording(). Also moved all keys to static constants to avoid per-request allocations.
Noah Patel (review): One more: in batched prefill, are we attributing reuse to the correct request? The earlier hit-attribution bug made me nervous.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. This instrumentation reads the same per-request accounting used by the fixed metrics path (post PR-18433). Added an integration assertion that in a batched prefill scenario, the sampled request sees only its own summary event values.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Looks good now. Thanks for consolidating events + bucketing. Approving.
